newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Sievert sees no need for rate rise soon.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Sievert sees no need for rate rise soon.

text.p: A favourable German inflation outlook and the likely demand for money in the economy means that there is no reason for the Bundesbank to tighten monetary policy any time soon, a Bundesbank council member said on Tuesday.

Olaf Sievert, who heads the regional central bank based in the eastern German city of Leipzig, said in a speech "...I see no reason which could give us grounds to take a firmer grip on the monetary reins".
He added, however, that it was hard to say whether there could be further scope for reductions in leading interest rates.
"Whether there is room to manoeuvre on the downside remains to be seen," he told a reception in Leipzig, according to the text of his speech which was released in advance.

Sievert said the outlook for German inflation continued to be favourable despite increases in raw materials prices. "The prospects for the future also look good," he said, noting annual German inflation is now running at around 1.4 percent.

This fact, together with expectations that money supply growth will slow in 1997, meant that the Bundesbank did not have to be too concerned about the fact that M3 money supply growth overshot the Bundesbank's target in 1996, he said.
"The overshooting of the goal is no reason for considerable concern given that the pace of money supply growth had already started to slow last spring," he said.
